sources.entry: TopOff - Menu bar app for Homebrew — a full beer mug when packages are fresh, half a mug when it's time to refill.

summary.one_liner: TopOff is a free, MIT-licensed native macOS menu bar app that checks for outdated Homebrew packages in the background and runs updates with one click.
summary.what_it_does: It periodically checks for outdated Homebrew packages and shows them in the menu bar, with a full or half-full mug icon indicating whether updates are pending. Users can run brew update and brew upgrade from the menu, update all packages or selected ones, and enable Greedy Mode to include auto-updating apps such as Chrome or Slack. After upgrades it runs brew cleanup, with an optional brew cleanup --prune=all style. It can retry protected cask upgrades after prompting for an admin password, keeps an update history, and shows live progress during runs. The README says the app updates itself via Sparkle and makes no telemetry calls beyond GitHub update checks.
use_cases: keep Homebrew packages up to date
update Homebrew casks from the menu bar
see outdated brew packages at a glance
clean up Homebrew cache after upgrades
how_to_run: Download the latest DMG from the project's releases and drag TopOff to Applications
Launch TopOff; it is signed and notarized by Apple
notable: Greedy Mode switches scheduled checks and upgrades to include auto-updating apps
Live progress view: click the menu bar icon during updates to see the current package
Automatic retry of update checks when network connectivity is restored after launch
Signed and notarized builds, with in-app updates via Sparkle
Optional deep cache prune (brew cleanup --prune=all) behind a confirmation step
caveats: Network connections seen in a firewall may belong to Homebrew child processes rather than TopOff
